Ligand 2 is an aminophenyl thioether pyrazole and ligand 1 an oxadiazole-benzofuran; both are inactive and neither has anything worth crossing over. Ligand 1 does have a terminal methoxy methyl at atom 0 over an acyclic bond, which is the anchor that keeps one carbon and discards the other 16. The molecule I want to rebuild first has no methyl in it, so I cannot reach it in a single call from this host - but I can get there in two. This step attaches the whole pharmacophore to the surviving methyl, giving the acetanilide form: a conjugated anilide N-H on a benzene, meta to an arylamine N-H whose pyridine carries a bromine at C4. That is the arrangement three runs have converged on, with the bromine being the discovery that ended the last run. The acetyl is only a placeholder; I will swap it for a cyclopropyl next, which is worth about 0.10 of activity over an acetyl and has the best synthetic accessibility of any cap I have measured.

The acetanilide form is in, and its QED of 0.9116 is actually higher than the cyclopropyl version I am heading for - worth noting, because it means the cap swap is a trade rather than a free win. But the acetyl costs about 0.10 of activity against a cycloalkyl, and at this activity level that is far more than the couple of hundredths of QED it returns. Atom 1 is the amide carbonyl and atom 0 the acetyl methyl over a non-ring bond, so I swap the methyl for a cyclopropyl. That gives N-{3-[(4-bromopyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopropanecarboxamide, the best molecule found in three runs at jnk3 0.60 and Phi 2.3799. Getting it into the population on the first episode means the next two generations refine from there rather than searching, which is what turned run 3 into an improvement on run 2.
